newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes firmer, PGMs watch Russia.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes firmer, PGMs watch Russia.

text.p: Gold prices edged higher on Wednesday to fix at a fresh four-week peak and the platinum group metals (PGMs) rose as concerns deepened over a strike threat at Russia's Norilsk mine and metallurgical plant.
"Gold tried to push through $355.00 in Hong Kong and when that failed it got sold down below $353 briefly," a dealer said.
Gold fixed at $353.85 per ounce, a fresh high since January 28 and up from $353.10 on Tuesday.

Dealers said the market's early choppiness was likely to give way to relative calm ahead of the over the counter (OTC) options expiry this afternoon and the Humphrey-Hawkins Testimony on the economy of U.S. Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan later.
Dealers said the OTC expiry was likely to focus on $355.00 calls while Greenspan would be watched for comments on U.S. inflation trends and signs of change in U.S. monetary policy.
However, they said market sentiment continued to improve from the nadir of a 3-3/4 year low on February 12 at $336.90.
"These are fickle markets and as soon as a (upward) trend was seen, it encouraged shorts to cover their positions and take their profits," a dealer said.
Further encouragement came from the suspicion that producer sell orders had been held off the market at $347 at $350 suggesting the gold miners saw a chance of higher prices in the short term.
Platinum cruised to its highest fixing since November 27 last year at $377.00 on the basis of fund buying encouraged by unresolved questions over Russian production and export issues.
Reports of a union official saying that Norilsk could be struck on March 15 came out just before the 0945 GMT fixing.
"Russia's supply problems are attracting fund business. Further supply disruption could be crucial," one dealer said.
Platinum was indicated at a steady $376.75/$377.75, up $2.75 and palladium was at $141.00/$142.00, up $0.50.
Palladium matched its fixing of February 13 of $141.25, its highest since March 27, 1996.
"We are still seeing consumer and fund buying in palladium due to the delayed Russia-Japan export talks," a dealer said.
A Russian official earlier this week said talks could start next month but dealers are doubtful if shipments could begin before April
Silver was subdued and indicated at $5.22/$5.24 up two cents.
